rules.quote: No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, except that any city or town that accepts this chapter may adopt rent control regulation that provides: (a) after six months from the date of the initial adoption of rent control regulation by a particular city or town, compliance on the part of property owners as to the rent control regulation or any subsequently adopted rent control regulation shall be entirely voluntary and uncoerced

baseline.explanation: The provided excerpts show no Massachusetts state law that limits rent increases. The state law that is in force, M.G.L. c. 40P, § 4, works the other way: it generally bars cities and towns from enacting, maintaining or enforcing rent control. The only exception is a narrow local option, and even then landlord compliance becomes entirely voluntary after six months. The 2026 rent control ballot question was blocked by the Supreme Judicial Court, so it is a failed measure and not law. Proponents mentioned a possible 2028 effort, which also does not count. The other Massachusetts excerpts (c. 186, §§ 11 and 31) cover notices to quit for nonpayment of rent, not rent increase limits. I have cited § 4 because it is the in-force state law that governs this question, not because it caps rents.
